beats.say: Every time a Linux program reads four KiB from disk or a socket with a classic syscall, the CPU slams across the user-kernel wall, saves registers, and flushes state. Modern NVMe drives finish millions of operations per second — turning syscalls into the bottleneck. Linux io_uring cuts those crossings all the way to zero.

Instead of passing one request per system call, io_uring maps two lock-free ring buffers directly into memory shared by both your application and the kernel. Your app writes sixty-four-byte submission entries into the Submission Queue and advances the tail pointer with a release store.

As the kernel finishes each read, write, or network accept, it writes a compact sixteen-byte completion entry into the Completion Queue and advances its tail. Your app reads completions straight out of user-space RAM with zero syscalls at all.

scenes.title: From thirty-two crossings to one, to zero

beats.say: With batching, an application drops thirty-two operations into the submission ring and makes one single enter syscall to hand them all over at once. Turn on SQPOLL, and a dedicated kernel thread polls the submission ring directly — dropping system calls per read all the way to zero, at the cost of burning a polling CPU core.

scenes.title: Below the rings: page cache vs direct I/O

beats.say: Submitting a read through io_uring does not automatically bypass the rest of Linux storage. With ordinary buffered I/O, a hot four KiB page returns straight from the kernel page cache in RAM, while a miss can hand off to an internal worker thread.

Add O_DIRECT with registered buffers, and that same four KiB read skips the page cache completely — traveling straight through the multi-queue block layer, blk-mq, into the NVMe drive's hardware queues with deterministic latency and zero extra memory copies.

That speed carries a security bill: io_uring is a second door into the kernel that bypasses per-syscall seccomp filters unless you lock down ring operations with explicit restrictions. When I/O rate is your bottleneck, io_uring is unmatched. Shared memory turns syscalls into pointers.
